item.title: Unforgettable: Unforgettable
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Emotional/Character-Based

Page Layout: Standard SCP format and addendum. The Addendum will have a journal where the main story takes place.

Elevator Pitch: My SCP shall be about a teen-aged boy (named Darcy Clover) who finds himself unable to be forgotten. All information about him has the same effect: when a person learns about it, it remains in their conscious memory forever. The memories can be ignored, but never forgotten.

The article's story will mainly revolve around Darcy's life when his anomaly manifested, shown through a digital journal he kept prior to his acquisition by the Foundation. According to his journal, Darcy was originally a normal high-school student, if a little introverted. When his anomaly manifested, however, he began to draw away from his friends and family, out of fear that they would remember him in a bad way.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The article begins with the boy's containment procedures, detailing many specific recommendations given by his lead psychologist. It then moves on to his description, noting (along with his effects) extremely antisocial tendencies and a general fear of cameras/microphones. It finally comes to a transcript of the boy's journal, where the core of the story lies.

The journal shows how he used to be a normal kid. He had mild feelings of self-doubt and issues socializing, but they never prevented him from living a normal life. That is, until his anomaly manifested. It's not known exactly when it happened, but he noticed how people began to act off around him. This "offness" became more intense over time, until people started to reference things he did that he had trouble remembering, leading him to realise that he was unable to be forgotten. He drew away from everyone he knew, drawing the attention of the Foundation as a consequence.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I personally haven't seen much relating to unforgettable anomalies, so I feel this would be somewhat new. My plan is to show how Darcy's anomaly changed his personal/social life for the worse, which I think would be interesting to read/write about.

Additional Notes: I tried to keep this as succinct as possible, so let me know if there's anything related to Darcy's anomaly or life that I forgot to explain or clarify. Please tell me if I should add anything else, too! :)


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: Axolotl: Re: Axolotl
item.content:encoded:
Thank you so much for your critiques! I’ve already started working on some changes.
On your first concern: I was thinking it would start with more of a “in person spottings”, then “research” (such as the carvings), and finally what work the foundation has done in regards to finding the creature.

Then on the second concern: I kind of get what you’re saying her, but I’ll need to think a little more on how to do that properly. The axolotl isn’t necessarily all knowing, it’s massive size and regenerative abilities on its own makes it a threat to be reckoned with. The axolotl can’t create life or summon an army of skeletons, it’s truly just a massive axolotl who’s natural healing abilities far surpass that of a normal one, with the mission of protecting earth.

Sorry if those didn’t make too much sense, I’m a little tired o_0

item.title: Blood Bowl Hell (Seeking Greenlight): Blood Bowl Hell (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Exploration

Elevator Pitch: An MTF explores an entrance to an underground hell filled with menstrual blood in Japan seemingly filled with souls of women tortured by oni (demons). It’s similar to the Buddhist “blood bowl sutra.” There, the MTF males start to show heightened misogyny, and begin to believe that women there are being rightfully punished. Eventually, a snakelike entity convinces the men to ritually sacrifice MTF women.

Central Narrative: Starts with local Shinto priest interview, warning of it and an entity underneath. Remains of Sarkic encampment nearby (split from Blood Lotus), but abandoned. MTF consists of a female team leader and predominantly male squad body. Historical quotes from sutra. They enter, and some MTF members recognize dead loved ones. They take a DNA sample from one for HQ to analyze. They discover distraught Sarkic woman, who attacks them, attracting the attention of oni. A group of people living there save them. The people state that they have a leader trying to pacify a slumbering female yaldabaoth-esque entity. The group experiences friction with the leader, especially when a group member breaks down after seeing dead family members, and those living in the SCP state that the women there are being punished for some unknown reason inherent to womanhood. The tension increases when one member of the group attacks the team leader and she kills him in defense.

+ show block
– hide block

People argue that her leadership caused it, and even question if women are temperamentally fit to lead. Eventually they arrive at the leader, and see that he is a snakelike being who wants to provide a human sacrifice seemingly to placate the sleeping entity. Male members sacrifice some women by tossing into blood pool, but team leader escapes. She runs into Sarkicist, who states that there is no slumbering being, the people living there were former members of her sect, and the serpent does sacrifices for his own power. They’re caught and killed. HQ discovers that DNA from “souls” match missing women, not deceased relatives, and people living in the hell close in the area during disappearance (i.e. kidnapping, MTF members were deceived). Remaining MTF males found in nearby city, despite entrance blocked off (ie multiple entrances/exits).

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Real-world religion ties, cult horror, social commentary, squick

Additional Notes: IK topics risky and may come off as sexist, but I’m taking care not to cross that line. IK compulsion’s frowned-upon, but this only accentuates pre-existing traits, hopefully keeping the horror.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: SCP Idea: {Redacted}: Re: SCP Idea: {Redacted}
item.content:encoded:
> Further thoughts < 
hide

The idea now is more developed, which is great to see. The idea that the staff know what the anomaly is but you don't could go in many directions with it. Some questions:

You cannot speak of it, cannot read it, cannot hear of it, and cannot see it.

You say later on that the staff know what the anomaly is, but can't convey it to you. How do they figure out if you can't perceive it? It could be interesting to see the ingenuity of the foundation staff in this case. Perhaps you could convey the actual anomaly subtly through the article (al la SCP-4428)

This SCP came into existence when a scientist attempted to document an anomaly he had discovered, only to realize he couldn't.

Did the antimemetic effects come from the interaction between the anomaly and the researcher? Or did were the effects already there? The wording here confuses me.

I would recommend that you tell reviewers what the actual anomaly is under the surface because I think an article would be more interesting if you could figure out what the anomaly is. Obviously, it doesn't have to be obvious, but antimemetic SCP's are often criticised for having no resolution, so I'd love to see what the anomaly is meant to be. Feel free to PM me if you revise the idea.

item.title: Scp 5133: Scp 5133
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes
Page Type: Scp Article
Elevator Pitch: Scp 5133 gets contained for an anomaly that has is blocked by personnel, as any description of appearance or behavior will cause the people involved to worship Scp 5133.

Central Narrative: Site 138 staff had all fallen into Scp 5133's memetic ability, no replies had been filed to site fund managers, two mtf operatives go to try to contain any escaped anomaly's after believing that site 138 had suffered a containment breach. They arrive and all scp's are contained except Scp 5133 where they report that it is memetic. Perfect containment cant be made as the original anomoly can be discovered and cared for if no information can be learnt.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The archived containment procedures are not what anyone would expect, as it states any personnel showing disliking to Scp 5133 are to be terminated via incinerator, and the archived description has been blocked by upper site command.

Additional Notes: Site 138 is just a random number I picked so finding a site that stores anomalies that could have been corrupted by a memetic hazard. And a site that can house things you dont know.

item.title: [Seeking Greenlight] Host of the Eldritch Abomination.: [Seeking Greenlight] Host of the Eldritch Abomination.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights:** Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror/Comedy

Elevator Pitch: A teenager name "Janual Grey" discovers that he's no longer a human after an unexplained blackout while he and his friends are at Acadia National Park, and later on woke up and finds himself into a reality-altering eldritch abomination.

+ show block
– hide block

Janual still acts like a regular human. However, discovering his powers has made a few changes. He possesses numerous anomalous properties that not even he knows how many does he has. And nature is every 24 hours passes by. If Janual doesn't consume any food that gives him the nutrition he needs, he will get driven into a state of absolute hostility, where he would go on a never-ending frenzy to satisfy his hunger, which of course that time he would begin to use more of his anomalous properties to lure humans deep into the woods. Which is why he usually lures bad peoples into his territory and consumes them.


Central Narrative:
+ show block
– hide block

The main point here is that:

Janual wasn't actually a human at all. Janual was born like this already. His father is a cosmic eldritch abomination worshiped by a cult named "Servants of "Darkness" " secretly built under a church where the cult mainly focuses on worshiping a deity named "Darkness". When the cult managed to make his father manifest into reality, he disguised himself as a handsome human. He seduced his mother into having a child when she visits the church during Christmas with Janual's grandmother. After borning out Janual, he de-manifest himself out of reality to let his son, Janual, destroy the world instead of him. However, due to embodying some human natures, Janual didn't become malevolent as his father was.

After a few years, Janual's mother had witnessed him consuming their neighbors in his monstrous form at the age of 3. As she started to find answers to why her son is like this, she soon discovers the truth. She could find a way to seal his powers from being unleashed due to worrying that he might bring apocalyptic events. However, during the past years, she slowly forgets about it.


Hook/Attention-Grabber: Janual is a friend in school with SCP-105 and is familiar with SCP-4051 as they've met each other before being held in Foundation custody.

Additional Notes: Draft is almost finished.
